newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks dragged sharply down by Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks dragged sharply down by Wall Street.

text.p: Mexican stocks closed sharply down on Friday after succumbing to a domino effect that spread from Wall Street throughout Latin American markets in the wake of strong U.S. sales and producer prices data.
"The bourse definitely slid due to developments on the Dow Jones," said Roberto Galvan, equity analyst at the Bursametrica consulting firm in Mexico City.
The leading IPC share index ended down 57.29 points, or 1.50 percent, at 3,764.46. Trading volume was moderate at 62.6 million shares.
The Dow Jones plunged 148.36 points to 6,391.69, while the U.S. 30-year Treasury bond was off 21/32 to yield 7.17 percent vs. 7.11 percent on Thursday.
In Brazil, the Bovespa index fell 2.21 percent to 9,518 points, while the Argentine Merval index plummeted 2.79 percent.
Dealers noted a lack of foreign investors in the market.

Traders said Telmex L shares weighed down the bourse most and accounted for 21 percent of all shares traded. The telecommunication firm's L class ended down 36 centavos (5 cents) at 15.84 pesos ($2.00), while its ADRs ended off 7/8 at 40 on Wall Street.

Financial Group GFB B class was another heavily traded decliner, off six centavos (1 cent) at 2.58 pesos (33 cents) on fears of interest rate hikes that would increase the group's past-due loans burden, traders said.
On the broad market, 102 stocks changed hands, of which decliners outnumbered gainers by 54 to 18.

Cement maker Grupo Cementos de Chihuahua was a prominent gainer, up 32 centavos (4 cents) to 7.82 pesos (99 cents) on expectations the U.S. Department of Commerce would lower anti-dumping tariffs levied on imports of Mexican cement.

Situr, tourist arm of the debt-burdened Sidek group, headed the losers' list, off three centavos (less than 1 cent) to 20 centavos (3 cents). Sidek also fell sharply, by three centavos (less than 1 cent) to 31 centavos (4 cents).
